screening_decisions.reason: While this is an RCT of a TCA (clomipramine) in adolescents comparing to placebo, the intervention was administered INTRAVENOUSLY (200 mg iv), not orally. The selection criteria specifically requires orally administered tricyclic drugs.
This RCT tests fluoxetine, which is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), not a tricyclic antidepressant. The selection criteria specifically requires tricyclic drugs.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of nortriptyline (a TCA) in adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range.
This is a qualitative review article, not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of imipramine (a TCA) in depressed children. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range (children).
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of amitriptyline (a TCA) in children aged 9-12 years with major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a Cochrane review about newer generation antidepressants (SSRIs), not a primary RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of imipramine (a TCA) in adolescents with comorbid anxiety and major depressive disorders. The comparison is imipramine+CBT vs placebo+CBT, which still compares TCA to placebo. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of imipramine (a TCA) in prepubertal children with major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range.

This RCT includes an imipramine (TCA) vs placebo arm for adolescent depression. While it also tests paroxetine, the imipramine arm meets the selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range.
This is a review article about mechanism of action, not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a review of overdose cases, not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis, not a clinical RCT. Does not meet any selection criteria.

This is a retrospective case series of amitriptyline poisoning/overdose cases, not a randomised controlled trial for depression treatment. The population is children with intoxication, not depressed children being treated.
This appears to be a secondary analysis examining predictors of treatment response rather than a primary RCT comparing TCA to placebo. The abstract does not describe randomization or a control group.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of desipramine (a TCA) in adolescents aged 13-18 years with major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article about psychopharmacology, not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This includes a double-blind, placebo-controlled study of imipramine (a TCA) in children/adolescents with school refusal and depression. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range.

This is a retrospective review of poison control center data on unintentional TCA ingestions, not a randomised controlled trial for depression treatment. The population is children with ingestions, not depressed children being treated.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of amitriptyline (a TCA) in adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a double-blind trial of clomipramine (a TCA) in children with school refusal and neurotic disorder. The abstract mentions relief of depression, indicating depressed children. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range.
This is a meta-analysis of trials, not a primary RCT. Additionally, the patients were aged 18-65 years (adults), outside the 6-18 age range.

This appears to be an observational study examining the relationship between plasma levels and response, not a randomised controlled trial comparing TCA to placebo. No placebo group or randomization is described.

This is a randomized, controlled trial of amitriptyline (a TCA) versus placebo in adolescents with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, oral TCA, placebo comparison, appropriate age range.

This is an 8-week double-blind study of imipramine (a TCA) versus placebo in adolescents. While the focus is on compliance, it is still an RCT comparing TCA to placebo in the appropriate population. Meets all selection criteria.
